Mike,

I never really needed earbuds until 2020 and the lockdowns. Your videos helped me choose the Jabra Elite 85t, and they were perfect. However, in 2023, about 2.5 years later, the battery started becoming an issue because I was a heavy user, wearing them for several hours every day.

My next earbuds were, once again, a pair of Jabras, this time, the Elite 7 Pro. I loved them and still have them, but after another 2.5 years, the battery life is no longer what it used to be. So I started wondering, “What comes next from Jabra?”

Unfortunately, as far as I know, Jabra is now only producing and selling one type of earbuds, the Evolve2, and they are considerably more expensive (almost $350) and not as good as the previous models (you dont even have them in your new videos as one of the good ones). So I decided to try another brand and bought the Sennheiser Momentum. It was a very bad decision. Once you get used to Jabra, it is surprisingly easy to be disappointed by earbuds in the same price range. My Sennheisers were bulkier, their ANC wasn't even close to being as good as my Jabras, and they weren't nearly as comfortable. And on top of that, after just one week, the left earbud died! I later learned that this wasn't an uncommon problem, as several users had experienced the same issue.

I have never appreciated my Jabras as much as I do now. So I just bought two pairs of older models, both brand new: the Jabra Elite 7 Pro ($315) and the Elite 85t ($181). That should give me Jabras for the next 5–6 years, hopefully long enough for another brand and model to come along that can truly match them.

One interesting thing I've noticed is that even used Jabras are surprisingly expensive, and there are actually several people offering battery replacement services for them.

I really hope Jabra reconsiders its decision to leave the consumer earbuds market. After trying several brands, including Bose, Apple, Sony, and (unfortunately) Sennheiser, I would say that the Elite 7 Pro were either the best or among the best earbuds I have ever used across virtually every category.

Did you know about the decline of Sennheiser's earbuds? I'd be very interested to hear your take on it.

Thank you for your videos!

Got a story to tell.

I’ve spent the last 2 years with the Motif IIs and absolutely loved them. Always loved the marshall style, I even have the big ol vintage marshall cabs my dad used to play on when he was young. They’re super old now but still loud asf. I thought those earbuds really shared that same marshall soul. Plus beyond just the aesthetic, that crocodile-texture finish gave them a pretty good ruggedness, never minded throwing the case in my pocket with coins or accidentally dropping it. Top of that the earbuds themselves had a solid grip that was perfect for the gym or running, really.

But here’s the thing: I lost them a month ago. I don’t think it was on the bus, because I always wait until I’m through my front door to take them out specifically so I don’t lose them. But I’ve searched every single inch of my house since then and haven't found a thing. House is clean now at least. But it’s been kind of a nightmare, spent weeks searching every corner because I just couldn't believe I’d lose them like that.

If I knew for a fact I left them on the bus I could just mourn them and move on BUT because I'm convinced they’re somewhere in my house… feel like I'm failing a game of hide n seek against it. Finally starting to face the reality but yk… still now every time I see a creepy shadow under the couch or feel something in a bag I’m hoping to feel that freakin crocodile skin only to be disappointed again. exhausting.

I’m finally caving and getting the airpods pro 2 instead of rebuying the Motif II. Most logical move ig, just don’t want this to happen again, the Find My of apple is pretty good with their U chips and all the transparency and noise cancelling stuff is better than the Motif IIs, definitely gonna miss the marshall aesthetic though. Just kinda feel like a white sheep buying airpods.
